text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight Ultra-Bright LED 36 Camera / Video Light with Rechargeable Battery Pack and Charger for Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Pentax DSLR, Mini-DSLR and Camcorders This is an great value in a light panel. While the size limits the amount of light output (compared with larger models made by Bestlight) the size makes this far more workable on smaller cameras.

I've used a couple of their larger models, and they are fine for hefty DSLRs. But, when put on a smaller camera it makes it so top-heavy that it topples over. This one, however, is so small and light (it is less than 2.5 inches wide and weights only 2.1 ounces including the battery) that it worked fine on my Powershot without making it top-heavy.

Now, the size does limit the light output – this is nowhere near as powerful as their larger models. It also does not have variable light output as the larger models do. It just has an on/off switch. But for general lighting tasks, it works very well.

It comes with an internal lithium battery that is rated at 1200mAh and a charger for the battery. The battery is small and adds little weight to the device. I find that to be a big plus, since many of their larger models don’t come with a battery. On the downside, this will not run on AA batteries like their larger models do, so when the battery is dead you’ll have some downtime until it recharges (unless you buy a spare battery).

It has a hot shoe attachment for mounting on the camera. It can also be mounted on a tripod or light stand. The mount is plastic but reasonably well made. Note: although it has a hot shoe, it does not communicate with the camera in any way. You have to manually turn it on/off.

It does not come with filters, so the color temperature is limited to 6500K. That's a good point for general use, however.

This is a great choice for smaller cameras or for when you want to add some light but don’t want to deal with a larger unit. It’s easy to toss into a camera bag and carry along. The performance is excellent and the build quality is quite good given the price (especially since a battery and charger is included). Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight Ultra-Bright LED 36 Camera / Video Light with Rechargeable Battery Pack and Charger for Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Pentax DSLR, Mini-DSLR and Camcorders

Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers When I first purchased the Kindle Paperwhite, I did so because I had an older Kindle (keyboard version) and some of the letters on the keyboard ceased working. I did a lot of research before I traded in my old Kindle. I really liked the reviews on the new Paperwhite version so decided to purchase it. I had to replace my first Paperwhite because the refresh screen turned every screen black. Customer service was excellent and when it was determined that we could not reset the kindle I received a new one. I waited until now to write this review (it was purchased earlier this year) because there were many differences and wanted to make sure that the review gave the Kindle what I felt it deserved.

First, I must say that I love many of the features of the Paperwhite version: it is small enough to fit in my purse, the font is easy on the eyes, the back-light is great in any light, the dictionary feature works well and I love the fact it has a vocabulary builder. It is very easy to download books and to access my library; it is also easy to locate different pages in the book.

However, the reason I rated the PaperWhite a 3 is because of the page turning (I have had no further problems with the refresh). Sometimes with light touch it will not turn the page or it will skip 3 or 4 pages and you have to back up to your last read page, which I find very annoying. I had more control with my older Kindle as it had a button on the side that allowed you to control the page turns and wish that the Paper White had the same feature. Other than this, the Paper White has a lot of great features but I am very disappointed with the page turn function.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

I dumped this watch and went back to a regular, inexpensive sports watch.
text_fidelity_b: woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)
